class: A long-running orchestrator session keeps growing its context past the 250k-token limit set by ADR-178, so every later turn re-sends a huge context and the orchestrator alone burns about half of the session's tokens.
mechanism: Nothing stops or restarts the session at a context size; the limit is prose (ADR-178 change 1) and the session runs on through several rows. Each turn, and each kit-guard block (2 turns), re-sends the whole context.

first_seen.where: chunk 3 session A a43256ae and chunk 4 session c097bcc4
first_seen.evidence: measure_process.py --session a43256ae: avg context 363k/turn over 627 turns (audit: 366k x 1,400 turns, 512M tokens, 17.3 h); audit_main.py for c097bcc4: 574 turns at an average of 312k = 179M tokens, 50% of the session's tokens (agents 178M); 16 / 20 kit-guard blocks at about 2 x 312k = ~10M per session.

fix: ADR-188 (2): a fresh orchestrator session about every 2 rows. ADR-178 tracker rows 1 and 18 (same counter: average context per turn < 250k).

detection.note: measure_process.py reports the number after the fact at session end (tracker row 1 is 'missed'); nothing stops a session at the limit.
